problem: Let $I=[1,2]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}=[0,2-i]\times {i}.$ Which of the following represents ${⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$
worked_solution:
Recall that the intersection of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *all* the sets:

$$
{⋂}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for all}\,\,k\in I}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=1,$ we have 

$$
{X}_{1}=[0,2-1]\times {1}=[0,1]\times {1}={(k,1)\,:\,k\in [0,1]}.
$$

This represents a horizontal line segment from the point $(0,1)$ to the point $(1,1)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/ddb7039dfcdbc2ef4070ce732c635a48194b6675cc3c78de6267e656c5e8387a.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}=[0,2-i]\times {i}={(k,i)\,:\,k\in [0,2-i]}
$$

is the horizontal line segment from the point $(0,i)$ to the point $(2-i,i).$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/e83644a2f0de96ee58ea893028bb7a42681ee71a15d194f2b344c4c15f60fafe.png)

There are no points that lie in all sets. Therefore, the intersection of the indexed sets is $∅,$ the empty set.
